preserved_objections.basis: The coupling of K-means clustering with grey association analysis is fundamentally flawed as K-means assumes spherical clusters and equal variance, while grey association is designed for small sample sizes with uncertain information, making their mathematical coupling theoretically unsound and likely to produce arbitrary point selections

The candidate fails to specify critical boundary conditions including spindle material properties, ambient temperature fluctuations, cooling system parameters, and machining loads that dramatically affect thermal behavior, making the screening mechanism unreliable across different operating environments

The provided evidence [doi:10.1016/j.aasri.2012.06.032] demonstrates that thermal gradients in high-speed spindles are highly dynamic and non-linear, contradicting the assumption that static clustering can identify consistently sensitive measurement points across warmup cycles

The candidate provides no evidence that the selected temperature points will capture the complex thermal deformation patterns better than existing full-field temperature monitoring methods, making it likely to perform equivalently or worse than the baseline approach

Installing additional temperature sensors at "key locations" identified by the algorithm would require intrusive modifications to the spindle housing that compromise structural integrity and create new thermal disturbance points, violating the fundamental requirement of non-interference with precision components

The testable prediction fails to account for the time lag between temperature measurement and actual spindle elongation, as well as the confounding effects of different thermal expansion coefficients in various spindle materials, making the correlation measurement fundamentally ambiguous
